species.real: The Severn estuary has one of the biggest tidal ranges in the world, and surfers ride the Severn Bore for miles inland, cheered on from the pub gardens.
species.name: Borelet

dex.text: A little hump of brown water that runs upstream when everything else is running down. Fishermen hear it coming as a hiss under the bridge.
dex.fact: A tidal bore is a wave that rolls upriver when a big incoming tide squeezes into a narrowing estuary. The River Trent, which flows into the Humber, has one, and locals call it the Aegir.

species.real: The Aegir is biggest on spring tides, which are nothing to do with spring: they are the extra-large tides just after a new or full moon.
species.name: Aegir

dex.text: Rides the spring tides up the Humber and into the Trent with a roar and a beard of foam. Boats in its path are lifted, spun and set down again, a bit further from home.
dex.fact: Aegir was the giant of the sea in Norse myth, and the Trent's tidal bore is named after him, perhaps a leftover from the Vikings who settled along the Humber. The biggest bores come with the spring tides near the equinoxes.
